name: Photogravure
summary: A carbon-tissue positive is transferred to a copper plate, which is etched through a dusted aquatint grain. The plate prints continuous photographic tone as deep, rich ink on thin tissue, with no visible screen.

philosophy.core_thesis: A photograph etched into copper through an aquatint grain prints as continuous tone in a deep ink. The photograph then reads as an original print.
design_principles: Expose a carbon tissue under a positive, transfer it to a copper plate and etch through 3–5 iron-chloride baths.
Etch the plate through a dusted aquatint grain, so that the tone shows no dots.
Print in one warm black or brown-black, wiped by hand.
Print on thin Japan tissue or laid paper, and keep the plate mark.
Keep the full tone scale: a deep velvet black, soft mid-tones and a clean light.
Mount the tissue on a larger sheet, with a margin of 20–40 mm.

process.matrix: Copper plate with resist and aquatint grain
process.image_making: Carbon tissue exposed under a positive, transferred, developed, etched through several iron-chloride baths

inks.strategy: One warm black or brown-black intaglio ink, wiped by hand so that each sheet differs a little.

screening.rule: Make the continuous tone through a dusted aquatint grain of about 150 grains an inch, which shows no regular dot.

registration.rule: One plate prints the image; a second plate can add a tone, with a shift of 0.3 mm.

substrate.stock: Japan tissue or thin laid paper, cream to buff.
substrate.finish: Thin and smooth, often chine-collé on a heavier mount.

surface.impression: A plate mark of 3–5 mm; the ink in the deep tones stands in light relief.
surface.sheen: Matt, with a rich depth in the darks.
surface.texture: A fine, random grain in the tones, and no dots.

marks: fine random aquatint grain, no dots

emotion.target_response: Hushed, artful reverence: the viewer sees a photograph that has the depth and weight of a print.

avoid_when: The design needs a sharp, high-contrast digital photo.

modifiers.how: Replace the photographic tone with stepped aquatint tones and hard stopped-out edges.
Print from a gelatin plate on matt paper, with a fine reticulation grain and no plate mark.
